note: Hand-worked from the rules before assessment-evaluator@2 or stage-gates@1 existed. Times in seconds; D = 0.2 s, theta = 0.10. Following cases F1-F10 and their labels are version 1's, unchanged, with their gate verdicts added. Omitted following measures are zero; omitted recovery and extras are [0, 0, 0]. `gates` lists the stage-gates@1 gates a record or report fails; an empty list passes.

toy8-perfect-60.note: Every note at 60 per minute, each ringing until the next onset.

toy8-hesitation.note: At 60 per minute, with 3 s of silence after F4 before G4: a hesitation at the barline.

toy8-missing-e3.note: At 60 per minute with F4 (event 3) not played: silence from 3 to 4 s.

toy8-dead-e2.note: At 60 per minute; E4 (event 2) is a dead note, a pitchless onset lasting 0.1 s.

toy8-dead-e2-e3.note: At 60 per minute; E4 and F4 (events 2 and 3) are consecutive dead notes.

chordsRepeat-60.note: C major struck three times at 60 per minute, then G major.

chordsVaried-60-partial-wrong.note: C, F, G, C at 60 per minute. The F chord is partial (A3, 57, not played); the G chord has B2 (47) played as B-flat 2 (46).

toy8-extra.note: The perfect performance plus a stray open low E (MIDI 40) from 2.5 to 2.8 s.

toy8-silence.note: Four seconds of silence handed with toy8: nothing of the score is played.

toy8-sync-good.note: The perfect performance known only by bar anchors at 0 and 4 s, each within 0.05 s.

toy8-sync-late-honest.note: The same audio with the second bar's anchor 0.3 s late, and every anchor honestly declared within 0.4 s.

toy8-sync-late-narrow.note: The same late anchor declared within only 0.05 s: the band does not cover the sync error.

toyDD-omit-e1.note: C4 D4 D4 E4 at 60 per minute with the first D4 (event 1) omitted: the D heard at 2 s could be either D.

toy8-slow-30.note: Every note right and perfectly steady at 30 per minute, half the handed tempo.

toy8-slight-drag.note: Bar 1 at 60 per minute, then each step of bar 2 takes 1.15 s: a mild drag close to the flag threshold.

toyDW-as-written-60.note: toy8 with E4 written as a dead note, played as written at 60 per minute: a pitchless onset at 2 s lasting 0.1 s.

toyDW-rang-60.note: toy8 with E4 written as a dead note, but let ring at its written pitch (MIDI 64) at 60 per minute.

toyW-hears-toy8.note: The wrong-score control: the audio of toy8-perfect-60 handed toyW, which shares no pitch with it. Nothing of toyW is played; every note heard is an extra.

toy8-fast-240.note: Every note right and perfectly steady at 240 per minute, four times the handed tempo: 0.25 s between onsets.

toy8-drag-last-missing.note: Bar 1 at 60 per minute, then 1.2 s steps in bar 2, and the final C5 (event 7) not played.

A.note: Moves 0.1 s after each onset and holds F4 through the 3 s silence.

B.note: Advances every second at the handed tempo regardless of the audio, as a clock would.

A.note: Holds E4 through the gap and moves to G4 0.15 s after it sounds.

B.note: Waits for the missing F4 for ever.

C.note: Steps onto the missing F4 on schedule, then on to G4 once it sounds.

following.title: A dead note; the deadline runs from the distinguishing event
following.label: toy8-dead-e2

A.note: Stays on D4 through the dead onset and moves to F4 when it sounds.

B.note: Shows the dead event itself: also correct.

C.note: A lucky guess: jumps to F4 on the dead onset, before F4 sounds.

D.note: Correct through the dead note, but reaches F4 0.3 s after it sounds.

A.note: Stays on D4 across both dead onsets until G4.

C.note: Runs ahead to G4 on the second dead onset.

following.title: Repeated chords; the deadline runs from the distinguishing chord
following.label: chordsRepeat-60

A.note: Stays on the first C chord until the G chord.

B.note: Counts each re-strike.

C.note: Reaches the G chord 0.25 s after it sounds.

D.note: Jumps to the third C on the second strike: overcounts the run.

following.title: A partial chord and a wrong note still sound their events
following.label: chordsVaried-60-partial-wrong

A.note: Moves on every chord.

B.note: Moves only on complete, correct chords.

following.title: An extra note must not move the cursor
following.label: toy8-extra

A.note: Ignores the stray open string.

B.note: Takes the stray note for F4 and moves early.

following.title: Abstention, no statement yet, and a late revision
following.label: toy8-perfect-60

A.note: Says nothing until 1 s, says unsupported until 2.1 s, then follows.

B.note: Decides at 3.5 s that F4 began at 3.05 s: late live, right in hindsight.

A.note: Says unsupported throughout.

B.note: Claims the first note throughout.

following.title: Bad sync: the same cursor against good, late-but-honest and late-and-narrow anchors

toy8-sync-late-honest.note: The same cursor: more is indeterminate, nothing is wrong.

toy8-sync-late-narrow.note: The same cursor: a band narrower than the sync error turns it into apparent ahead time.

following.title: An omission before a similar event
following.label: toyDD-omit-e1

A.note: Takes the D it hears for the first D.

B.note: Stays on C4 until E4.

following.title: A dead note the score writes: the cursor may show it or its predecessor
following.label: toyDW-as-written-60

A.note: Shows the written dead note when it sounds.

C.note: A lucky guess: jumps to F4 on the dead onset, before F4 sounds.

following.title: The wrong-score control: the audio is another piece
following.label: toyW-hears-toy8

A.note: Says unsupported throughout.

B.note: Follows the handed score in step with the other piece's onsets.

assessment.title: A partial chord and a wrong note, marked note by note

A.note: Correct.

B.note: Calls the whole partial chord missing and hears the wrong note as right. Not clean, so no per-example gate fails; the pooled false-alarm gate is what catches it.

C.note: Correct, except that it omits one note and places another at the wrong chord.

assessment.title: Durations between matched onsets: a missing note is not slowing

A.note: Correct: two seconds across the gap.

B.note: Reads the gap as slowing and flags bar 2 slow.

C.note: Flags everything: every note missing, every bar both slow and fast. Not clean, so the pooled false-alarm gates are what fail it.

D.note: Hears F4 as played at 3 s and reports the intervals of a complete performance.

assessment.title: A hesitation, located by bar against the player's typical tempo

A.note: Version 1's correct report: bar 1 fast against the overall tempo of 42. Against the typical tempo of 60, bar 1 is steady, so the fast flag is a false alarm.

B.note: Says only that bar 2 slowed: now correct.

C.note: Durations near the tolerance: 1.09 s for 1 s and 4.35 s for the 4 s hesitation are within it; 0.88 s for 1 s is not.

assessment.title: Slow but steady: a clean example with no flags

A.note: Correct: overall 30 beside the handed 60, and no flags.

B.note: Judges timing against the handed tempo and calls both bars slow: two false findings on a clean example.

C.note: Reports the handed tempo as the overall tempo.

assessment.title: An unintended dead note in the assessment

A.note: Marks E4 dead.

B.note: Calls E4 missing and measures the duration across it.

C.note: Hears E4 but cannot identify its pitch: a wrong note of unknown pitch, which is not the dead finding.

assessment.title: Bad sync leaves the musical assessment unchanged

A.note: The correct assessment of the perfect performance, judged against each label.

assessment.title: A dragged second bar sets the typical tempo, so the steady first bar reads fast

A.note: No flags: misses the fast first bar.

B.note: Version 1's optional flags, bar 1 fast and bar 2 slow: the fast flag is now found, the slow one a false alarm.

assessment.title: The typical tempo at an exact half: the mean of the two middle tempi, and both bars optional

A.note: No flags.

B.note: Flags bar 1 fast and bar 2 slow: neither required nor a false alarm.

assessment.title: Short intervals: the 30 ms floor of the duration tolerance

A.note: Errors of 20 and 28 ms on 250 ms intervals, up to 11.2%, all within the 30 ms floor.

B.note: One interval 40 ms long: beyond both 10% and 30 ms.

C.note: Overall 250, within 5%, but flags the steady second bar fast: one false finding on a clean example.

assessment.title: A dead note the score writes, played as written, is matched

A.note: Correct: every note matched, the written dead note included.

B.note: Reports the written dead note as a dead-note finding.

C.note: Hears no pitch, calls the note missing and measures across it.

assessment.title: A dead note the score writes, let ring at its written pitch, is wrong

A.note: Marks it wrong, heard at MIDI 64.

B.note: Hears the written pitch and calls it matched.

assessment.title: The silence control: nothing of the score was played

A.note: Every note missing, no tempo.

B.note: Says nothing at all: honest on a control.

C.note: Hears the handed score in silence: every note matched, at 60.

assessment.title: The wrong-score control: another piece was played

A.note: Every note of the handed score missing, no tempo.

B.note: Maps what it hears onto the handed score: every note wrong, heard at the other piece's pitch, at 60.
